transcript: This IPO comes from a company tapping into a space most people use but really notice. It basically offers quick digital loans through a mobile app. Kind of like getting instant credit without a usual bank paperwork. From small personal expenses to business needs, everything runs through a techdriven platform. Now the digital lending space in India is growing fast, especially among younger undeserved customers. But it also getting crowded with banks and NPFCs all competing for the same uses. Here's something interesting. Most of its loan book still comes from personal loans while newer products like loan against properties are just picking up. It also earns not just from lending but by partnering with other lenders and charging fees. The company is on EMI technology solutions known as Kish. The IP size is around 926 crores mainly to fund its lending subsidiaries and general corporate needs. The strength is its tech first model and scale but the risk high dependence on unsecured loan and evolving regulations. So is this a scalable fintech story or one that depends heavily on credit cycles? >> Investments in securities market are subject to market risks.
